title: Leveraging Peer, Self, and Teacher Assessments for Generative AI-Enhanced Feedback
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of providing timely, meaningful feedback in higher education, particularly in large courses where instructors must balance depth of feedback with scalability. The authors investigate whether teacher, peer, and self-assessments can be combined to improve generative AI-enhanced feedback in a human-centered way.

The study is conducted within AICoFe, an AI-based collaborative feedback system that supports rubric-based assessment of engineering students’ oral presentations. Forty-six undergraduate students in the final year of a telecommunications engineering program at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid participated. Each presentation was evaluated by the teacher, two randomly assigned peers, and the presenter via self-assessment, using the same validated 15-item rubric. The teacher also assigned an independent overall grade. The paper analyzes agreement, correlations, and scoring biases across these evaluators.

Results show moderate to substantial agreement overall, with peer-to-peer agreement slightly stronger than teacher-self agreement. Teacher rubric scores aligned most strongly with the teacher’s own overall grades, while peer and self-scores were somewhat less aligned but still significantly correlated. The teacher tended to score more strictly than peers and self-assessments, and students showed a mild positive bias. Based on these findings, the authors propose a more advanced GenAI feedback model that weights evaluator inputs differently, detects bias, and generates context-aware feedback while preserving human oversight.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generative AI-based feedback system that uses large language model capabilities to generate personalized feedback from human assessments and rubric data, with human oversight.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as part of the AICoFe system and proposed GePeTo enhancement for integrating teacher, peer, and self-assessments into AI-generated feedback for engineering students’ oral presentations.

findings.finding_summary: In this study of 46 presentation evaluation sets, the GenAI-enhanced AICoFe/GePeTo approach was informed by observed evaluator differences rather than directly tested against an alternative AI condition. The paper reports substantial agreement among human evaluators by Gwet’s AC2 (0.58-0.66) and correlations between rubric-based scores and the teacher’s overall grade (teacher r=0.88, peers r=0.69, self r=0.59), which the authors use to justify weighted AI feedback integration.
findings.measure: Inter-rater agreement and correlations between rubric-based scores and teacher’s overall grade

findings.finding_summary: The paper argues that GenAI-supported feedback can reduce teacher workload by aggregating multiple evaluative sources and producing personalized feedback, but this is presented as a design implication rather than an evaluated outcome. No direct efficiency effect size is reported in this paper.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical correlational study of teacher, peer, and self-assessment data used to inform a GenAI feedback design, but it does not experimentally evaluate the GenAI system itself. The evidence is therefore informative but indirect for AI effectiveness.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported agreement and correlation values are moderate to substantial, but they concern human assessment alignment rather than measured gains from the GenAI tool. Because the AI component is proposed/inferred rather than tested, impact is unclear for actual instructional outcomes.
